features.title: IDE rule block written once
features.journey: In a new temporary folder with a `.cursor/rules/` folder and an AGENTS.md that has one line of user text, run `python -m autopilot init` twice. The Cursor rule file and AGENTS.md each contain the Autopilot block exactly once (with `ap status`, `ap next`, `ap start`), and the user's line in AGENTS.md is unchanged.
features.evidence: Setup: a temp folder with .cursor/rules/ and an AGENTS.md containing 'my own line'. I ran `python -m autopilot init` twice. The first run printed 'append   AGENTS.md'; the second printed 'keep     AGENTS.md'. A new .cursor/rules/autopilot.mdc was created with frontmatter (alwaysApply: true) and one block between <!-- autopilot:begin --> and <!-- autopilot:end -->.
